cities.name: Amritsar
cities.overview: The spiritual centre of Sikhism, close to the Pakistan border, known for the Golden Temple, its food and the Attari–Wagah border ceremony.
cities.history: Founded by Guru Ram Das in the 16th century around a sacred pool, and the spiritual centre of Sikhism ever since. It suffered the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in 1919 and the upheaval of Partition in 1947.

cities.name: Anandpur Sahib
cities.overview: A holy town in the Shivalik foothills of Rupnagar district, where the Khalsa was founded in 1699.

cities.name: Patiala
cities.overview: A former princely capital, known for its fort, its turbans, its salwars and its generous pegs.
cities.history: Founded by Ala Singh in the 18th century, and for two centuries the seat of the Sikh Maharajas of Patiala.

cities.name: Fatehgarh Sahib
cities.overview: A town near Sirhind, sacred for the martyrdom of the younger sons of Guru Gobind Singh.

cities.name: Harike
cities.overview: A village at the meeting of the Beas and Sutlej, known for its wetland.

cities.name: Kapurthala
cities.overview: An old princely capital known as the Paris of Punjab, for its French-style palace and gardens.

places.name: Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib)
places.shortDescription: Sikhism's holiest gurdwara, its gilded sanctum set in a sacred pool, open to everyone day and night.
places.description: Sri Harmandir Sahib rises from the middle of the Amrit Sarovar, the pool of nectar, reached by a causeway from the marble walkway that surrounds it. Hymns from the Guru Granth Sahib are sung continuously from early morning until night. The langar, the community kitchen, serves free meals to tens of thousands of people of every faith each day, cooked and served largely by volunteers. Cover your head, remove your shoes and wash your feet before entering. Visit early morning or late night for the calmest experience.
places.history: The temple was built under the fifth Guru, Arjan Dev, and completed in 1604, when the Guru Granth Sahib was first installed. It was rebuilt after attacks in the 18th century, and Maharaja Ranjit Singh covered its upper storeys with gold in the early 19th century.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. Gurpurab and Diwali, when the temple is lit, are especially beautiful.

location.address: Golden Temple Road, Atta Mandi, Katra Ahluwalia, Amritsar, Punjab 143006

places.name: Jallianwala Bagh
places.shortDescription: Memorial garden at the site of the 1919 massacre, a turning point in India's freedom struggle.
places.description: Jallianwala Bagh is a walled garden a short walk from the Golden Temple. A flame-shaped memorial stands at its centre, bullet marks are preserved in the surrounding walls, and the Martyrs' Well recalls those who jumped in to escape the firing. Galleries tell the story of the massacre and its aftermath, and an evening light-and-sound show runs most days. Entry is through the same narrow lane the troops used.
places.history: On 13 April 1919, Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered troops to fire on a crowd gathered in the garden, killing hundreds of unarmed people. The massacre turned many Indians against British rule. The memorial was inaugurated in 1961.

location.address: Golden Temple Road, Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, Punjab 143006

places.name: Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib
places.shortDescription: The gurdwara at Anandpur Sahib marking the birthplace of the Khalsa, one of the five Takhts of Sikhism.
places.description: Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib stands on a hill in Anandpur Sahib, its white domes visible across the town. It marks the spot where Guru Gobind Singh created the Khalsa, and it keeps weapons associated with the Guru. The town comes alive at Hola Mohalla, held the day after Holi, when Nihang Sikhs display martial arts, horsemanship and mock battles. The Virasat-e-Khalsa museum nearby, with its striking modern architecture, tells the story of Sikh history.
places.history: On Baisakhi day in 1699, Guru Gobind Singh initiated the first five members of the Khalsa here, the Panj Pyare.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. Hola Mohalla falls in March, the day after Holi.

places.name: Attari-Wagah Border
places.shortDescription: The India and Pakistan land border near Amritsar, famous for its evening flag-lowering ceremony.
places.description: Each evening, soldiers on both sides stage a high-kicking ceremony before a cheering crowd. Arrive early to get a seat.
places.history: The ceremony has been held daily since 1959.

places.name: Partition Museum
places.shortDescription: A moving museum in Amritsar's Town Hall on the 1947 Partition, told through survivors' memories.
places.description: Photos, letters and recorded stories tell of the millions displaced by Partition. It's in a restored building close to the Golden Temple.

places.name: Gobindgarh Fort
places.shortDescription: A restored fort in the centre of Amritsar, once held by Maharaja Ranjit Singh and the army.
places.description: Long in army hands and now open to visitors, with museums, Punjabi food stalls and a live show on Punjabi history.
places.history: Strengthened by Maharaja Ranjit Singh in the early 19th century.

places.name: Durgiana Temple
places.shortDescription: A Hindu temple in Amritsar with a sacred lake, built in a style echoing the Golden Temple.
places.description: A silver-doored temple in the middle of a tank, reached by a bridge. Its layout will feel familiar if you've seen Harmandir Sahib.

places.name: Virasat-e-Khalsa
places.shortDescription: A striking modern museum of Sikh history at Anandpur Sahib, designed by Moshe Safdie.
places.description: Two wings of curved, steel-topped buildings reflected in pools, with galleries that take you through 500 years of Sikh history.

places.name: Gurdwara Fatehgarh Sahib
places.shortDescription: The gurdwara at the place where the younger sons of Guru Gobind Singh were martyred.
places.description: A large white shrine marks where the two boys were bricked up alive. The Shaheedi Jor Mela in December is a major event.

places.name: Qila Mubarak, Patiala
places.shortDescription: The old fortified palace of the Maharajas of Patiala, in the heart of the city.
places.description: A large walled fort with a palace, a Darbar Hall museum and bazaars crowding its gates. Restoration is ongoing.

places.name: Harike Wetland
places.shortDescription: A Ramsar wetland where the Beas and Sutlej meet, with huge winter flocks of migratory birds.
places.description: One of north India's largest wetlands, and a major stop for ducks, gulls and terns. The rare Indus river dolphin lives in the Beas nearby.

places.name: Kapurthala
places.shortDescription: A former Sikh princely capital with a Versailles-style palace and a Moorish mosque.
places.description: The Jagatjit Palace, now a school, was modelled on Versailles. The Moorish Mosque, built by a French architect, is modelled on Marrakesh's Koutoubia.
